title: Building, mechanical, fuel-gas and electrical permits for a glass studio's furnace, glory hole, kilns and exhaust
question: I am fitting out a building in Staunton with a gas-fired glass furnace, glory hole, kilns, torches and exhaust. Which building and trade permits do I need, how do I apply, what do they cost, and what inspections follow?
office: Community Development Department, Building Services Division (the Building Official and inspectors; City Hall, 3rd floor)
summary: Fitting out a hot shop is commercial construction under the Virginia Uniform Statewide Building Code, which Staunton's Building Services Division enforces. A change of use to a shop with gas-fired furnaces and kilns, any new walls, structural work, exhaust and make-up air, gas piping, fuel tanks, electrical service and fire protection all need permits before work starts: a building permit (commercial alteration or change of use) plus separate mechanical, gas, electrical and, if any, plumbing, fire suppression and fire alarm permits. Since May 5, 2026 applications go through the city's online portal with PDF plans; the city estimates fifteen business days for commercial review. The building permit application asks for the use group, construction type and occupant load; the trade permit application asks the gas type (natural gas, above-ground or in-ground LP), the number of fuel tanks and commercial hoods, and the electrical service size, and commercial trade work needs square footage and estimated cost. Fees are set in City Code § 15.10.120 (read on eCode360): commercial alteration $0.18 per square foot with a $95 minimum, each trade permit $0.05 per square foot with a $95 minimum, storage tank installations $200 per tank, fire alarm $250, sprinklers $0.08 per square foot ($150 minimum), plan review before application $200, certificate of occupancy for an existing building $95, temporary commercial certificate $250 for 60 days. A Certificate of Appropriateness comes first in a historic district, real estate taxes must be paid, a new water or sewer connection needs the Engineer's application, and the certificate of occupancy issues within five working days after the final inspection is approved.

legal_basis.quote: Such building code shall supersede the building codes and regulations of the counties, municipalities and other political subdivisions and state agencies.
Enforcement of the provisions of the Building Code for construction and rehabilitation shall be the responsibility of the local building department.
Any building or structure may be inspected at any time before completion, and shall not be deemed in compliance until approved by the inspecting authority.
Fees may be levied by the local governing body in order to defray the cost of such enforcement and appeals.

In the event that a local building department denies an application for the issuance of a building permit, the local building department shall provide to the applicant a written explanation detailing the reasons for which the application was denied.

It shall be unlawful for the building official or other authority to issue or allow the issuance of such permits unless the applicant has furnished his license or certificate number issued pursuant to this chapter or evidence of being exempt from the provisions of this chapter.
Application for a permit shall be made to the building official and a permit shall be obtained prior to the commencement of any of the following activities

Installations or alterations involving (i) the removal or addition of any wall, partition, or portion thereof; (ii) any structural component; (iii) the repair or replacement of any required component of a fire or smoke rated assembly; (iv) the alteration of any required means of egress system, including the addition or removal of emergency supplemental hardware; (v) water supply and distribution system, sanitary drainage system, or vent system; (vi) electric wiring; (vii) fire protection system, mechanical systems, or fuel supply systems; or (viii) any equipment regulated by the USBC.
In addition, the building official may authorize work to commence pending the receipt of an application or the issuance of a permit.
In no case shall an applicant be required to appear in person.

An application for a permit for any proposed work shall be deemed to have been abandoned six months after the date of filing unless such application has been pursued in good faith or a permit has been issued
A permit or any amendments to an existing permit shall not be issued until the designated fees have been paid, except that the building official may authorize the delayed payment of fees.

A building official shall be permitted to revoke a permit if work on the site authorized by the permit is not commenced within six months after issuance of the permit or if the authorized work on the site is suspended or abandoned for a period of six months after the permit is issued

Under circumstances where the building official is unable to make the inspection or test required by Section 113.3 or 113.4 within two working days of a request or an agreed upon date or if authorized for other circumstances in the building official's written policy, the building official shall accept reports for review.

The building official shall issue the certificate of occupancy within five working days after approval of the final inspection and when the building or structure or portion thereof is determined to be in compliance with this code and any pertinent laws or ordinances, or when otherwise entitled.

steps.step: Confirm that the work needs permits (it does) and list them
steps.who: Studio owner, designer and contractors; Building Services Division
steps.how: Under the state building code a permit is needed before removing or adding walls, structural work, altering exits or fire-rated assemblies, plumbing, electric wiring, fire protection, mechanical systems, fuel supply systems or any equipment the code regulates, and before a change of occupancy. A hot shop fit-out touches most of these: the furnace, glory hole and kilns and their exhaust and make-up air (mechanical), the natural gas or propane piping and any tank (gas), the electrical service for kilns, blowers and lighting (electrical), any sinks or cold-shop drains (plumbing), and any sprinkler or alarm work (fire suppression, fire alarm). Staunton lists the commercial building permit types as new commercial, addition/alteration, multi-family, swimming pools, fire suppression/fire alarm, preliminary plan review, elevators, solar, generators, sign footers and change of use; trade permits are separate.
steps.deadline: Before work starts; emergency equipment replacement by the end of the first working day after it begins
steps.quote: Separate permits are required for electrical, plumbing, mechanical, and gas.

steps.step: Clear the prerequisites: zoning, historic review, taxes, utilities, asbestos
steps.who: Studio owner; Planning & Zoning; Historic Preservation Commission; City Treasurer; City Engineer; Environmental Programs
steps.how: The permit is issued only when the plans show the work will meet building and zoning rules, so settle the use with Planning & Zoning first (glass_studio_zoning_use). In a historic district the commercial permit page says a Certificate of Appropriateness is required before the building permit. Real estate taxes on the property must be paid. A new or larger water or sewer connection needs the Water and Sewer Connection and Facility Fees application to the City Engineer before any building permit (glass_studio_utilities_and_environment). Alterations to an existing building need the Asbestos Regulations Compliance Form; buildings first permitted before 1985 that are renovated for commercial purposes need the state asbestos inspection certification. Site work over 10,000 square feet needs a land disturbing permit.
steps.deadline: Before the building permit is issued
steps.quote: All real estate property taxes must be paid prior to issuance of a building permit.

steps.step: Optional: ask for a preliminary building permit review of the plans
steps.who: Studio owner or designer; Building Services Division
steps.how: For a design with unusual equipment (a gas-fired furnace running continuously, a glory hole, kilns, oxygen and propane) it can pay to submit the plans for the city's Preliminary Building Permit Review for Commercial Projects before applying. It is a plan review only, estimated at fifteen business days, with comments posted in the portal; the building permit is a separate submittal. City Code § 15.10.120 (read on eCode360) sets the fee at $200.
steps.fee: $200.00 (plan review prior to permit application; City Code § 15.10.120, read on eCode360)
steps.quote: This is a plan review only. To obtain a building permit for the project is a separate submittal process.

steps.step: Prepare the plans: use group, occupant load, equipment, exhaust, gas and electrical
steps.who: Studio owner with an architect or engineer (sealed drawings are usual for commercial work); equipment suppliers
steps.how: The building permit application asks for the Virginia Construction Code year, present use, construction type, use group, number of stories, occupant load and whether there is fire suppression or an alarm. For a hot shop with a gallery and classroom the designer must classify the spaces (the building official's certificate of occupancy will state the group classification) and show separations, exits and ventilation. Plans must be no larger than 24 by 36 inches and show the complete scope, floor plans with existing and proposed layouts, wall sections, elevations and the foundation; a site sketch shows property lines, setbacks, structures, mechanical equipment, parking and distances. Include the furnace, glory hole and kiln specifications, combustion air and exhaust, gas piping sizes and pressures, any tank or cylinder storage, the electrical service size and the Commercial Construction E-codes design criteria; a ComCheck energy report is optional. Digital plans go in the portal or to permits@fileshare.ci.staunton.va.us with the project address in the subject line.

steps.step: Apply for the building permit online (or on paper at City Hall)
steps.who: Owner, licensed contractor or an agent with the owner's written consent; Building Services Division
steps.how: Since May 5, 2026 new applications go through the online portal: create an account (an existing Business License or Personal Property Tax account works), enter the project details and upload PDF plans. Paper applications are still accepted at the Community Development office (City Hall, 3rd floor). A contractor gives a Virginia contractor license number and expiration date and the email used on the portal; a permit cannot issue without the license number or an exemption statement. Choose Commercial as the type of use and Alteration and/or Change of Use as the permit type, give the square footage and value of construction, and describe the work. The city estimates fifteen business days for commercial review; if more information is needed you are emailed and resubmit in the portal (the city publishes resubmittal guides). A denial must come with written reasons. An application not pursued is abandoned after six months.
steps.deadline: City estimate fifteen business days for commercial permits
steps.fee: Commercial alteration or interior up-fit $0.18 per square foot, $95.00 minimum; new commercial building $0.22 per square foot to 5,000 square feet then $0.12, $95.00 minimum (City Code § 15.10.120, read on eCode360); plus the state 2% levy
steps.quote: Estimated Processing Time: Fifteen (15) business days.

steps.step: Apply for the mechanical and gas permits for the furnace, glory hole, kilns and exhaust
steps.who: Licensed mechanical or gas contractor (or the owner where exempt); Building Services Division
steps.how: Apply online or on the Trade Permit Application, marking Commercial and giving the square footage and estimated cost. The mechanical section asks for the number of fuel tanks to be installed and the number of commercial hoods, and requires heating and cooling equipment for non-residential spaces to be sized under the 2021 Virginia Energy Conservation Code § C403.3.1. The gas section asks the type of gas (above-ground LP, in-ground LP or natural gas), whether an appliance is being changed out and whether it will be vented. Fuel-fired glass furnaces, glory holes and kilns are equipment regulated by the code, so their installation, venting and combustion air are inspected; a propane tank also brings the Fire Marshal's LP-gas permit (glass_studio_fire_permits). The city estimates one business day for trade permits unless historic approval is needed; the permit is void if work does not start within six months.
steps.deadline: Before the trade work starts; permit void if construction is not started within six months of issuance
steps.fee: Commercial alteration mechanical and gas permits $0.05 per square foot each, $95.00 minimum each; new commercial $0.08 per square foot, $95.00 minimum; storage tank installations $200.00 per tank; commercial hood or hood suppression $150.00 per hood (City Code § 15.10.120, read on eCode360)
steps.quote: Commercial projects, provide square footage: _______________ Estimated cost of work: $________________

steps.step: Apply for the electrical permit (and plumbing, fire suppression or fire alarm permits if needed)
steps.who: Licensed electrical, plumbing or fire protection contractor; Building Services Division
steps.how: The electrical section of the Trade Permit Application asks for the size of service and the electric service provider; kilns, blowers, cold-working equipment and compressors often drive a service upgrade. Plumbing asks whether city services serve the site, whether an easement is needed and how many exterior lines are installed. Fire suppression and fire alarm sections ask the type of system, the number of sprinkler heads for an alteration and the dialer types; the Fire Suppression / Fire Alarm permit type needs fire plans and is estimated at fifteen business days.
steps.fee: Commercial alteration electrical or plumbing permit $0.05 per square foot, $95.00 minimum; fire suppression $0.08 per square foot, $150.00 minimum; fire alarm installation $250.00; water line or sewer line $95.00 each (City Code § 15.10.120, read on eCode360)

steps.step: Pay the fees and receive the permits by email
steps.how: No building code permit is issued until the fees in City Code ch. 15.10 are paid (the building official may allow delayed payment). Fees are paid in the portal or at the office by card, check or cash. The approved permit is emailed and lists the minimum inspections. Refunds: 75% of the fee above the minimum if no work has started; half if 50% or less of the work is done; none beyond that; a permit renewal is $25 (§ 15.10.120(d), read on eCode360).
steps.fee: As calculated under City Code § 15.10.120; permit renewal $25.00 each
steps.quote: Once the permit has been approved, the applicant will receive the permit by email. At that time, inspections can be requested through the online portal.

steps.step: Build, then request each inspection in the portal
steps.who: Permit holder and contractors; Building Services inspectors
steps.how: Post the permit and keep a set of approved plans on site. Request inspections in the online portal when each stage is ready: framing and fire-rated assemblies before concealment, mechanical and gas rough-in (piping pressure tests), electrical rough-in, plumbing rough-in, exhaust and ventilation, and the finals for each trade and the building. The inspector approves in writing or lists defects to correct and reinspect ($50 reinspection fee under § 15.10.120, read on eCode360). If the city cannot inspect within two working days of a request, it must accept a third-party report under the building official's written policy. Statement of Special Inspections forms apply where the code requires special inspections.
steps.deadline: At each stage before the work is covered
steps.quote: When construction reaches a stage of completion that requires an inspection, the permit holder shall notify the building official.

steps.step: Get the certificate of occupancy (or a temporary one) before opening
steps.how: After the final inspections are approved the building official issues the certificate of occupancy within five working days; it states the code edition, group classification, construction type and whether a sprinkler system is provided. A temporary certificate can be requested before the work is complete if the space is safe to occupy; City Code § 15.10.120 (read on eCode360) prices a commercial temporary certificate at $250 for 60 days and a certificate of occupancy for an existing building at $95. The Fire Marshal's operational permits and inspection run alongside (glass_studio_fire_permits).
steps.deadline: Certificate issued within five working days after the approved final inspection
steps.fee: Commercial temporary certificate of occupancy $250.00 for 60 days; certificate of occupancy for an existing building $95.00 (City Code § 15.10.120, read on eCode360)
steps.quote: Upon the request of a permit holder, a temporary certificate of occupancy may be issued before the completion of the work covered by a permit

caveats: City pages and forms are Internet Archive copies (capture dates in sources); the current Building Permit Application (639168510357930000) has no archive copy, so the earlier version is cited. The live pages may have changed.

Fee amounts come from a reading of City Code § 15.10.120 on eCode360 on 2026-10-19 and are reported as figures; eCode360's terms forbid reproducing its text, so no section is quoted. Confirm with Building Services before budgeting.

Which occupancy group(s) a hot shop with gallery and classroom falls in, whether a furnace and glory hole are treated as industrial furnaces or fuel-fired appliances, and whether sprinklers, rated separations, make-up air or a hood are required, are design and plan-review questions under the 2021 Virginia Construction Code, Mechanical Code and Fuel Gas Code that this file does not answer.
Trade permit processing is quoted by the city as one business day on the residential side; the commercial trade permit time is not stated separately.
The city's Required Inspections handout read earlier is a residential list; the inspections for a commercial fit-out are those listed on the permit.

Whether the Fire Marshal's Office reviews the plans for compressed gas and LP-gas storage as part of the building permit, or only through its own operational permits, was not stated on the pages read.
